rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies oxidation and phase evolution during heating of a different alloy (AlCrCoFeNi) under controlled atmospheres, while the target paper studied tribo-corrosion of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in water at various temperatures. These are fundamentally different kinds of studies.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses heating in air/vacuum with HTXRD tracking, whereas the target paper uses immersed reciprocating tribo-corrosion in deionized water at 25–100 °C. The conditions are completely different and do not overlap.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes selective oxidation and Al depletion-driven phase transformation, while the target paper's mechanism involves temperature-dependent competition between depassivation, repassivation, and tribo-layer stability during wear-corrosion. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts oxidation scale thickness and subsurface phase transformation, while the target paper predicts wear volume, friction coefficient, and tribo-corrosion rate as a function of temperature. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
